reopened.actual_B_display: Your written count puts the tap on the next 1. In the worked example, find the bar line after the half note. The note lasts through 2 and 3, and the new note starts on the very next beat, 1. The bar line takes no time. In your try, 3 is silent, but it still gets a full beat. Listen to your take around that silent 3. Does the tap land on 3 or on the next click, the new 1? You can keep your answer private.

material.worked: Play a quarter note on count one, hold a half note through counts two and three, then start a new note on the next one. The bar line itself takes no time.
material.lesson: Use a comfortable three-beat pulse on open A. Continue counting through silence and let the count return to one at the bar line. If playing becomes uncomfortable, stop and trace the bars on paper.
material.excerpt: On this card a bar holds three quarter-note beats. Keep a silent beat’s place even when it ends a bar. The next bar starts on the very next beat.

material.worked: In a bar of four, an open D lasting two beats, a one-beat rest and a final quarter note fill the bar. The first note occupies counts one and two. Count three silently and begin the last note on four.
material.lesson: Count one, two, three, four with a comfortable click. Bow a single open string on the marked sounds and leave the rests silent. Put the violin down if playing feels uncomfortable. You can continue by counting or marking beats on paper.
material.excerpt: For this card a click is a quarter-note beat. Keep the count going during a rest. A two-beat note begins once and continues across the next click.
